rules.decision: A causal question must pass an explicit identification gate before Methodome recommends a causal estimator.
conditions: User/protocol seeks an effect, impact, intervention effect, or other counterfactual contrast
rules.action: Require a defined intervention/exposure, outcome, target population, causal estimand, and defensible identification assumptions before method selection.
assumptions: Exchangeability or a design/strategy that justifies the relevant exchangeability condition
warnings: Do not convert an ordinary observational association model into a causal claim merely by adjusting for covariates.
Causal identification and statistical estimation are separate problems.
exceptions: Randomized assignment changes the identification argument but does not remove the need to define the estimand and analysis population.

source_evidence.support: Hernán and Robins organize observational causal identification around exchangeability, positivity and consistency, and explain that randomization is expected to produce exchangeability.

rules.decision: Difference-in-differences requires a defensible equal/parallel trends assumption and should not be suggested from before/after data alone.
conditions: Treated and comparison groups observed over time
Program assignment is not simply individual randomization
rules.action: Consider difference-in-differences only when the design supports a credible comparison group and the equal-trends assumption is addressed.
assumptions: Equal/parallel untreated outcome trends across groups over the relevant pre-intervention period
No design violations that invalidate the comparison
warnings: A pre/post comparison without a credible comparison group is not difference-in-differences.

source_evidence.support: World Bank guidance gives difference-in-differences its own chapter and explicitly identifies the equal-trends assumption and method limitations.

rules.decision: Primary analysis variables and their operational definitions should be prespecified before outcome-driven analysis decisions.
conditions: A protocol/SAP defines primary and secondary objectives or outcomes
rules.action: Capture primary versus secondary status, operational outcome definition, analysis population, and planned analysis before locking the Methodome plan.
diagnostics: Check whether primary-variable definition changed after data review
warnings: Post-hoc redefinition of a primary variable can introduce bias and multiplicity problems.

source_evidence.support: ICH E9 states that the precise primary-variable definition should be specified in the protocol and warns against post-hoc redefinition.

rules.decision: Methodome analysis plans should separately record analysis sets, missing-data handling, estimation/testing, multiplicity, subgroup/covariate plans, and sensitivity analyses where applicable.
conditions: An analysis plan is being created or locked
rules.action: Represent these elements explicitly rather than burying them in free text.
warnings: A method name alone is not a complete analysis plan.
exceptions: Not every project requires every field; applicability should follow design and objectives.

source_evidence.support: ICH E9 Section V treats these as separate data-analysis considerations.
Gamble et al. provide a minimum-content framework for SAPs aimed at transparency and reproducibility.
